_comment: Facts about this adapter that its probe response cannot carry: display names, maturity, and the engine versions CI actually restores from. Everything the probe declares (adapter version, engine id, source kinds, pitr) is read from testdata/probe_response.golden instead — never duplicated here. The capabilities generator fails if the source names below do not match the probe exactly, and the integration suite restores from the image listed under verified — the baseline on every run — so neither can drift. The official image idles under `command: sleep infinity` (its entrypoint passes a non-arangod command through, measured) and the adapter starts the server itself, with the engine's own TTL thread held back for the drill. The image is Alpine-based and ships no bash, so every script this adapter runs is `sh` (measured). The server reached readiness at a 768 MiB cap, which is the lightest of the recent engines. Licence position: the Community licence permits internal business use within a dataset below 100 GB; see docs/engine-licensing.md and the adapter README. conformance_verified is false and stated rather than quietly omitted: §10 check 9 provisions 64 KiB of random bytes as the source and expects a restore, and this adapter's artifact is an arangodump output whose dump.json names the database to restore into. A random file names none, and inventing one would restore into a database the backup never mentioned. Twelve of the fifteen checks pass; the other two are that one's cascade. See docs/capabilities.md and docs/engine-versions.md.
name: ArangoDB

sources.arangodb_dump_tar: One tar archive (plain or gzip) of an `arangodump` output, its files at the root or under one wrapping directory
sources.arangodb_dump_dir: A directory of `arangodump` outputs; the one whose own dump.json claims the newest instant is restored
